page: Amazon Web Services r5ad.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.2 GHz. The memory subsystem provides 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage includes 600 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 5 Gbps, and no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented toward memory capacity rather than peak single-threaded computational power. In CPU benchmarks, the AMD EPYC 7571 demonstrates lower single-core metrics, achieving 590.9 in stress-ng single-core and 726.0 in Geekbench single-core, both placing in the bottom tier. However, multi-core metrics scale to 4582.0 in Geekbench and 12505.34 in PassMark CPU score, reflecting average performance across concurrent threads. Memory bandwidth ranges from 620.46 GB/sec for small cached blocks down to 27.3 GB/sec for uncached read blocks.

The qualitative cost profile favors workloads that require large RAM footprints and fast temporary NVMe storage without paying a premium for cutting-edge CPU compute. Operations such as Redis caching reach 9.89 million SET operations per second, and PassMark database operations score at an average 3727.21. Due to the modest per-core throughput, this instance is best matched with in-memory caching layers, relational database replicas, batch data processing, and stateful memory-bound analytical jobs requiring local scratch disks.
description: Amazon Web Services r5ad.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Nitro hypervisor. It is equipped with an AMD EPYC 7571 processor delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores at 2.2 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of DDR4-3000 memory. The instance bundles 600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps, with zero GPUs included. Benchmark testing indicates modest single-thread performance alongside steady multi-core capabilities, achieving 4582.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 9.89 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. The 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and direct NVMe storage offer cost-efficient memory density, making the r5ad.4xlarge well suited for in-memory databases, Redis caches, analytical processing, and memory-heavy database workloads that benefit from fast local storage.
